faqs.question: What does the Galactomannan, Aspergillus Antigen Test by EIA – BAL Fluid measure?
faqs.answer: This test detects galactomannan antigen in bronchoalveolar lavage (BAL) fluid.

faqs.question: Why is the Galactomannan, Aspergillus Antigen Test by EIA – BAL Fluid done?
faqs.answer: • To diagnose Aspergillus infections, especially in individuals with weakened immune systems. • To monitor the effectiveness of treatment for Aspergillus infections. • To guide the duration of antifungal therapy. • To identify patients at risk for invasive fungal infections.

faqs.question: When is the Galactomannan, Aspergillus Antigen Test by EIA – BAL Fluid recommended and who should take the test?
faqs.answer: This test may be recommended for: • Individuals with weakened immune systems, such as those with HIV/AIDS or undergoing organ transplantation. • Patients with suspected or confirmed fungal infections, especially Aspergillus infections. • Those undergoing treatment for Aspergillus infections to monitor response.

faqs.question: What if the results of the Galactomannan, Aspergillus Antigen Test by EIA – BAL Fluid are abnormal?
faqs.answer: An abnormal result indicates the presence of Aspergillus infection or other conditions that affect galactomannan levels. Elevated levels of galactomannan may suggest an active Aspergillus infection. Abnormal results do not necessarily indicate cancer or any other serious condition.

faqs.question: What to expect during the Galactomannan, Aspergillus Antigen Test by EIA – BAL Fluid?
faqs.answer: During the test: • A sample of bronchoalveolar lavage (BAL) fluid will be collected using a sterile, leak-proof container. • The sample will be sent to the laboratory for testing. • The laboratory will use the enzyme immunoassay (EIA) method to measure galactomannan levels in the BAL fluid sample.

faqs.question: What preparations are required before the Galactomannan, Aspergillus Antigen Test by EIA – BAL Fluid?
faqs.answer: To prepare for this test: • Discuss your clinical history and any prescribed medications with your doctor. • Follow any specific instructions given by your healthcare provider. • No dietary or fasting restrictions are typically required. Please reach out to your healthcare provider for any specific requirements.

faqs.question: What other tests may be ordered with the Galactomannan, Aspergillus Antigen Test by EIA – BAL Fluid?
faqs.answer: Other tests that may be recommended alongside the Galactomannan, Aspergillus Antigen Test by EIA – BAL Fluid include: • Fungal culture: This test is performed to isolate and identify the specific fungus responsible for the infection. • Imaging studies: Chest X-ray or CT scan may be done to evaluate the extent of lung involvement.

faqs.question: What is the Galactomannan, Aspergillus Antigen Test by EIA – BAL Fluid also known as?
What is an Aspergillus infection?
faqs.answer: Aspergillus infection is a fungal infection caused by the Aspergillus fungus. It commonly affects the lungs but can also occur in other organs. In individuals with weakened immune systems, these infections can be severe or life-threatening.
